forgotten_high_value.one_line: 80KB approved implementation plan (16 tasks, all complete) for a battle-tested autonomous multi-agent loop reliability architecture — the single richest forgotten harness artifact in this slice.
load_bearing_ideas: Supervisor OUTSIDE the failure domain: the recovery supervisor must not live in the same runtime it recovers (WSL) — use kernel-level Windows Task Scheduler (already independently adopted by the harness as MCPAgentMailSupervisor + agent-monitor; CORROBORATES).

3-watchdog taxonomy: dead-process (Task Scheduler restart) + alive-but-stuck (log-freshness 10min) + lock-contention (lock-age 30min); termination classes consecutive_failures / loop_stale / loop_thrashing / stall>15min. Concrete impl of AGENTS.md §4a-longrun / §4b-two-strikes + feedback_workflow_orchestration 'hung agent deadlock, detect by write-freeze'.

Layered bypass prevention: prompt rule (Layer 1) + PreToolUse hook returning permissionDecision:deny (Layer 2) = ~95% bypass-resistant. Mirrors the harness PreToolUse exit-2-block model (AGENTS.md §6).

Durable broker + per-hat append-only ndjson spool + idempotent event envelope {event_id uuidv7, parent_event_id, run_id, iteration, attempts, status} with single-writer discipline + at-least-once retry. Relevant to mcp_agent_mail / workflow-orchestration message bus.
max_activations:30 per-agent kill switch = runaway-cycle prevention (anti-grind).

Single-actor-per-phase discipline: no two agents act on shared mutable state in the same phase (they interfere) — corroborates feedback_parallel_agent_worktree 'shared-worktree contamination'.
Phase-gated hats: every action agent reads phase.json first and no-ops unless it is the phase it serves.
